--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). title: >- [Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Split the nodes into two halves with few edges between them (Kernighan-Lin). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L47399-L47575){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.kernighan_lin_bisection( partition=None, max_iter=10, weighted=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Kernighan-Lin bisection](../assets/graphs/kernighan-lin-bisection.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two squares with a diagonal, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edges D to E and C to F. Left, the starting split you pass, A, B, E, F (teal) against C, D, G, H (violet), cuts 8 edges, in the accent color. Right, after swapping pairs of nodes the halves are A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, and only the two accent edges D to E and C to F are cut, a cut size of 2.0." width="100%"} The Kernighan-Lin heuristic (1970) improves a two-way split by swapping pairs of nodes between the halves whenever that reduces the number (or weight) of edges cut, keeping the halves the same size. It is the classic method for balanced graph bisection: dividing a circuit between two chips, a computation between two processors, or a network into two communities of equal size. Applied recursively, it partitions into more parts. Edge direction is ignored. Without `partition=`, the start is a random half; use `seed=` for reproducible results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [partition]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[list, list] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional starting split as two lists of nodes (IDs or labels) covering every node. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of improvement passes (default 10). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to minimize cut weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the starting half. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[set[int], set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The two halves as sets of node IDs (the first evolves from `partition[0]` when a partition is given). Their sizes differ by at most one, or keep the sizes of `partition`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or `partition` is not a split of all nodes. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pass tentatively moves, alternately from each side, the unlocked node with the largest gain (external minus internal weight), locks it and updates its neighbors' gains, then keeps the prefix of swaps with the largest total gain; passes repeat while they improve the cut. A pass costs $O(V^2)$ here. Follows NetworkX's `kernighan_lin_bisection`. NetworkX occasionally accepts a pass whose gain is zero up to rounding (which only exchanges the two sides) and then continues, so on some graphs the two end in different local optima. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~cut_size`) : The number of edges between the two halves. [](`~spectral_modularity_bipartition`) : Split in two by modularity, with no size constraint. [](`~greedy_node_swap_bipartition`) : Refine a split by modularity, with no size constraint. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two squares with a diagonal, joined by two edges. The starting split cuts 8 edges, and swapping nodes between the halves brings the cut down to the two edges between the squares: ::: {#1e282844 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "G"), ("G", "H"), ("H", "E"), ("E", "G"), ("D", "E"), ("C", "F"), ]) start = (["A", "B", "E", "F"], ["C", "D", "G", "H"]) left, right = graph.kernighan_lin_bisection(partition=start) ( sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in left), graph.cut_size(list(left)), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], 2.0) ``` ::: ::: ### Halving the karate club Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33), and the `faction` attribute records which side each member joined. The factions have 16 and 18 members, while Kernighan-Lin keeps the two halves the same size. Counting the members of each half by faction: ::: {#f6f825b2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ec.karate_club().layout_kamada_kawai() left, right = karate.kernighan_lin_bisection(seed=1) karate.set_node_attrs("half", 0) karate.set_node_attrs("half", 1, nodes=list(right)) ( karate.get_node_df() .group_by("half", "faction") .len() .sort("half", "faction") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

The split cuts as few friendships as the factions do: ::: {#ea834c46 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} instructor_side = ( karate.get_node_df().filter(pl.col("faction") == 1)["id"].to_list() ) karate.cut_size(list(left)), karate.cut_size(instructor_side) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (10.0, 10.0) ``` ::: ::: ### From a random start With `max_iter=0`, no pass runs and the random starting half comes back (left): it cuts 37 edges. The first pass already brings the cut down to 10 (right): ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#466f3a99 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} start, rest = karate.kernighan_lin_bisection(max_iter=0, seed=1) karate.set_node_attrs("start", 0) karate.set_node_attrs("start", 1, nodes=list(rest)) karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="start", edge_color_by="start", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
